    98→// diffLines compares two strings and returns line-level diff stats.
    99→// Returns (unchanged, added, removed) line counts.
   100→func diffLines(checkpointContent, committedContent string) (unchanged, added, removed int) {
   101→	// Handle edge cases
   102→	if checkpointContent == committedContent {
   103→		return countLinesStr(committedContent), 0, 0
   104→	}
   105→	if checkpointContent == "" {
   106→		return 0, countLinesStr(committedContent), 0
   107→	}
   108→	if committedContent == "" {
   109→		return 0, 0, countLinesStr(checkpointContent)
   110→	}
   111→
   112→	dmp := diffmatchpatch.New()
   113→
   114→	// Convert to line-based diff using DiffLinesToChars/DiffCharsToLines pattern
   115→	text1, text2, lineArray := dmp.DiffLinesToChars(checkpointContent, committedContent)
   116→	diffs := dmp.DiffMain(text1, text2, false)
   117→	diffs = dmp.DiffCharsToLines(diffs, lineArray)
   118→
   119→	for _, d := range diffs {
   120→		lines := countLinesStr(d.Text)
   121→		switch d.Type {
   122→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffEqual:
   123→			unchanged += lines
   124→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffInsert:
   125→			added += lines
   126→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffDelete:
   127→			removed += lines
   128→		}
   129→	}
   130→
   131→	return unchanged, added, removed
   132→}
   133→
   134→// countLinesStr returns the number of lines in a string.
   135→// An empty string has 0 lines. A string without newlines has 1 line.
   136→// This is used for both file content and diff text segments.
   137→func countLinesStr(content string) int {
   138→	if content == "" {
   139→		return 0
   140→	}
   141→	lines := strings.Count(content, "\n")
   142→	// If content doesn't end with newline, add 1 for the last line
   143→	if !strings.HasSuffix(content, "\n") {
   144→		lines++
   145→	}
   146→	return lines
   147→}
   148→
   149→// CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated computes final attribution using accumulated prompt data.
   150→// This provides more accurate attribution than tree-only comparison because it captures
   151→// user edits that happened between checkpoints (which would otherwise be mixed into the
   152→// checkpoint snapshots).
   153→//
   154→// The calculation:
   155→// 1. Sum user edits from PromptAttributions (captured at each prompt start)
   156→// 2. Add user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head diff)
   157→// 3. Calculate agent lines from base → shadow
   158→// 4. Estimate user self-modifications vs agent modifications using per-file tracking
   159→// 5. Compute percentages
   160→//
   161→// Note: Binary files (detected by null bytes) are silently excluded from attribution
   162→// calculations since line-based diffing only applies to text files.
   163→//
   164→// See docs/architecture/attribution.md for details on the per-file tracking approach.
   165→func CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(
   166→	baseTree *object.Tree,
   167→	shadowTree *object.Tree,
   168→	headTree *object.Tree,
   169→	filesTouched []string,
   170→	promptAttributions []PromptAttribution,
   171→) *checkpoint.InitialAttribution {
   172→	if len(filesTouched) == 0 {
   173→		return nil
   174→	}
   175→
   176→	// Sum accumulated user lines from prompt attributions
   177→	// Also aggregate per-file user additions for accurate modification tracking
   178→	var accumulatedUserAdded, accumulatedUserRemoved int
   179→	accumulatedUserAddedPerFile := make(map[string]int)
   180→	for _, pa := range promptAttributions {
   181→		accumulatedUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded
   182→		accumulatedUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved
   183→		// Merge per-file data from all prompt attributions
   184→		for filePath, added := range pa.UserAddedPerFile {
   185→			accumulatedUserAddedPerFile[filePath] += added
   186→		}
   187→	}
   188→
   189→	// Calculate attribution for agent-touched files
   190→	// IMPORTANT: shadowTree is a snapshot of the worktree at checkpoint time,
   191→	// which includes both agent work AND accumulated user edits (to agent-touched files).
   192→	// So base→shadow diff = (agent work + accumulated user work to these files).
   193→	var totalAgentAndUserWork int
   194→	var postCheckpointUserAdded, postCheckpointUserRemoved int
   195→	postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile := make(map[string]int)
   196→
   197→	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
   198→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   199→		shadowContent := getFileContent(shadowTree, filePath)
   200→		headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
   201→
   202→		// Total work in shadow: base → shadow (agent + accumulated user work for this file)
   203→		_, workAdded, _ := diffLines(baseContent, shadowContent)
   204→		totalAgentAndUserWork += workAdded
   205→
   206→		// Post-checkpoint user edits: shadow → head (only post-checkpoint edits for this file)
   207→		_, postUserAdded, postUserRemoved := diffLines(shadowContent, headContent)
   208→		postCheckpointUserAdded += postUserAdded
   209→		postCheckpointUserRemoved += postUserRemoved
   210→
   211→		// Track per-file removals for self-modification estimation
   212→		if postUserRemoved > 0 {
   213→			postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile[filePath] = postUserRemoved
   214→		}
   215→	}
   216→
   217→	// Calculate total user edits to non-agent files (files not in filesTouched)
   218→	// These files are not in the shadow tree, so base→head captures ALL their user edits
   219→	nonAgentFiles := getAllChangedFilesBetweenTrees(baseTree, headTree)
   220→	var allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles int
   221→	for _, filePath := range nonAgentFiles {
   222→		if slices.Contains(filesTouched, filePath) {
   223→			continue // Skip agent-touched files
   224→		}
   225→
   226→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   227→		headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
   228→		_, userAdded, _ := diffLines(baseContent, headContent)
   229→		allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles += userAdded
   230→	}
   231→
   232→	// Separate accumulated edits by file type using per-file tracking data.
   233→	// This is precise because accumulatedUserAddedPerFile tells us exactly which files
   234→	// the user edited between checkpoints.
   235→	var accumulatedToAgentFiles, accumulatedToNonAgentFiles int
   236→	for filePath, added := range accumulatedUserAddedPerFile {
   237→		if slices.Contains(filesTouched, filePath) {
   238→			accumulatedToAgentFiles += added
   239→		} else {
   240→			accumulatedToNonAgentFiles += added
   241→		}
   242→	}
   243→
   244→	// Agent work = (base→shadow for agent files) - (accumulated user edits to agent files only)
   245→	totalAgentAdded := max(0, totalAgentAndUserWork-accumulatedToAgentFiles)
   246→
   247→	// Post-checkpoint edits to non-agent files = total edits - accumulated portion (never negative)
   248→	postToNonAgentFiles := max(0, allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles-accumulatedToNonAgentFiles)
   249→
   250→	// Total user contribution = accumulated (all files) + post-checkpoint (agent files) + post-checkpoint (non-agent files)
   251→	totalUserAdded := accumulatedUserAdded + postCheckpointUserAdded + postToNonAgentFiles
   252→	totalUserRemoved := accumulatedUserRemoved + postCheckpointUserRemoved
   253→
   254→	// Estimate modified lines (user changed existing lines)
   255→	// Lines that were both added and removed are treated as modifications.
   256→	totalHumanModified := min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)
   257→
   258→	// Estimate user self-modifications using per-file tracking (see docs/architecture/attribution.md)
   259→	// When a user removes lines from a file, assume they're removing their own lines first (LIFO).
   260→	// Only after exhausting their own additions should we count removals as targeting agent lines.
   261→	userSelfModified := estimateUserSelfModifications(accumulatedUserAddedPerFile, postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile)
   262→
   263→	// humanModifiedAgent = modifications that targeted agent lines (not user's own lines)
   264→	humanModifiedAgent := max(0, totalHumanModified-userSelfModified)
   265→
   266→	// Remaining modifications are user self-modifications (user edited their own code)
   267→	// These should NOT be subtracted from agent lines
   268→	pureUserAdded := totalUserAdded - totalHumanModified
   269→	pureUserRemoved := totalUserRemoved - totalHumanModified
   270→
   271→	// Total net additions = agent additions + pure user additions - pure user removals
   272→	// This reconstructs the base → head diff from our tracked changes.
   273→	// Note: This measures "net new lines added to the codebase" not total file size.
   274→	// pureUserRemoved represents agent lines that the user deleted, so we subtract them.
   275→	totalCommitted := totalAgentAdded + pureUserAdded - pureUserRemoved
   276→	if totalCommitted <= 0 {
   277→		// Fallback for delete-only commits or when removals exceed additions
   278→		// Note: If both are 0 (deletion-only commit where agent added nothing),
   279→		// totalCommitted will be 0 and percentage will be 0. This is expected -
   280→		// the attribution percentage is only meaningful for commits that add code.
   281→		totalCommitted = max(0, totalAgentAdded)
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	// Calculate agent lines actually in the commit (excluding removed and modified)
   285→	// Agent added lines, but user removed some and modified others.
   286→	// Only subtract modifications that targeted AGENT lines (humanModifiedAgent),
   287→	// not user self-modifications.
   288→	// Clamp to 0 to handle cases where user removed/modified more than agent added.
   289→	agentLinesInCommit := max(0, totalAgentAdded-pureUserRemoved-humanModifiedAgent)
   290→
   291→	// Calculate percentage
   292→	var agentPercentage float64
   293→	if totalCommitted > 0 {
   294→		agentPercentage = float64(agentLinesInCommit) / float64(totalCommitted) * 100
   295→	}
   296→
   297→	return &checkpoint.InitialAttribution{
   298→		CalculatedAt:    time.Now().UTC(),
   299→		AgentLines:      agentLinesInCommit,
   300→		HumanAdded:      pureUserAdded,
   301→		HumanModified:   totalHumanModified, // Total modifications (for reporting)
   302→		HumanRemoved:    pureUserRemoved,
   303→		TotalCommitted:  totalCommitted,
   304→		AgentPercentage: agentPercentage,
   305→	}
   306→}
   307→
   308→// estimateUserSelfModifications estimates how many removed lines were the user's own additions.
   309→// Uses LIFO assumption: when a user removes lines from a file, they likely remove their own
   310→// recent additions before touching agent lines.
   311→//
   312→// See docs/architecture/attribution.md for the rationale behind this heuristic.
   313→func estimateUserSelfModifications(
   314→	accumulatedUserAddedPerFile map[string]int,
   315→	postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile map[string]int,
   316→) int {
   317→	var selfModified int
   318→	for filePath, removed := range postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile {
   319→		userAddedToFile := accumulatedUserAddedPerFile[filePath]
   320→		// User can only self-modify up to what they previously added
   321→		selfModified += min(removed, userAddedToFile)
   322→	}
   323→	return selfModified
   324→}
   325→
   326→// CalculatePromptAttribution computes line-level attribution at the start of a prompt.
   327→// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint BEFORE the agent makes changes.
   328→//
   329→// Parameters:
   330→//   - baseTree: the tree at session start (the base commit)
   331→//   - lastCheckpointTree: the tree from the previous checkpoint (nil if first checkpoint)
   332→//   - worktreeFiles: map of file path → current worktree content for files that changed
   333→//   - checkpointNumber: which checkpoint we're about to create (1-indexed)
   334→//
   335→// Returns the attribution data to store in session state. For checkpoint 1 (when
   336→// lastCheckpointTree is nil), AgentLinesAdded/Removed will be 0 since there's no
   337→// previous checkpoint to measure cumulative agent work against.
   338→//
   339→// Note: Binary files (detected by null bytes) in reference trees are silently excluded
   340→// from attribution calculations since line-based diffing only applies to text files.
   341→func CalculatePromptAttribution(
   342→	baseTree *object.Tree,
   343→	lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree,
   344→	worktreeFiles map[string]string,
   345→	checkpointNumber int,
   346→) PromptAttribution {
   347→	result := PromptAttribution{
   348→		CheckpointNumber: checkpointNumber,
   349→		UserAddedPerFile: make(map[string]int),
   350→	}
   351→
   352→	if len(worktreeFiles) == 0 {
   353→		return result
   354→	}
   355→
   356→	// Determine reference tree for user changes (last checkpoint or base)
   357→	referenceTree := lastCheckpointTree
   358→	if referenceTree == nil {
   359→		referenceTree = baseTree
   360→	}
   361→
   362→	for filePath, worktreeContent := range worktreeFiles {
   363→		referenceContent := getFileContent(referenceTree, filePath)
   364→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   365→
   366→		// User changes: diff(reference, worktree)
   367→		// These are changes since the last checkpoint that the agent didn't make
   368→		_, userAdded, userRemoved := diffLines(referenceContent, worktreeContent)
   369→		result.UserLinesAdded += userAdded
   370→		result.UserLinesRemoved += userRemoved
   371→
   372→		// Track per-file user additions for accurate modification tracking.
   373→		// This enables distinguishing user self-modifications from agent modifications.
   374→		if userAdded > 0 {
   375→			result.UserAddedPerFile[filePath] = userAdded
   376→		}
   377→
   378→		// Agent lines so far: diff(base, lastCheckpoint)
   379→		// Only calculate if we have a previous checkpoint
   380→		if lastCheckpointTree != nil {
   381→			checkpointContent := getFileContent(lastCheckpointTree, filePath)
   382→			_, agentAdded, agentRemoved := diffLines(baseContent, checkpointContent)
   383→			result.AgentLinesAdded += agentAdded
   384→			result.AgentLinesRemoved += agentRemoved
   385→		}
   386→	}
   387→
   388→	return result
   389→}

    27→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user for a yes/no confirmation via /dev/tty.
    28→// This works even when stdin is redirected (e.g., git commit -m).
    29→// Returns true for yes, false for no. If TTY is unavailable, returns the default.
    30→// If context is non-empty, it is displayed on a separate line before the prompt.
    31→func askConfirmTTY(prompt string, context string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    32→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing
    33→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
    34→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    35→	if err != nil {
    36→		// Can't open TTY (e.g., running in CI), use default
    37→		return defaultYes
    38→	}
    39→	defer tty.Close()
    40→
    41→	// Show context if provided
    42→	if context != "" {
    43→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s\n", context)
    44→	}
    45→
    46→	// Show prompt with default indicator
    47→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
    48→	var hint string
    49→	if defaultYes {
    50→		hint = "[Y/n]"
    51→	} else {
    52→		hint = "[y/N]"
    53→	}
    54→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s %s ", prompt, hint)
    55→
    56→	// Read response
    57→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
    58→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
    59→	if err != nil {
    60→		return defaultYes
    61→	}
    62→
    63→	response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
    64→	switch response {
    65→	case "y", "yes":
    66→		return true
    67→	case "n", "no":
    68→		return false
    69→	default:
    70→		// Empty or invalid input - use default
    71→		return defaultYes
    72→	}
    73→}

    75→// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
    76→// If the message contains only our trailer (no actual user content), strip it
    77→// so git will abort the commit due to empty message.
    78→//
    79→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
    80→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CommitMsg(commitMsgFile string) error {
    81→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from git hook
    82→	if err != nil {
    83→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
    84→	}
    85→
    86→	message := string(content)
    87→
    88→	// Check if our trailer is present (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
    89→	if _, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); !found {
    90→		// No trailer, nothing to do
    91→		return nil
    92→	}
    93→
    94→	// Check if there's any user content (non-comment, non-trailer lines)
    95→	if !hasUserContent(message) {
    96→		// No user content - strip the trailer so git aborts
    97→		message = stripCheckpointTrailer(message)
    98→		if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
    99→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   100→		}
   101→	}
   102→
   103→	return nil
   104→}
   105→
   106→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   107→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   108→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   109→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   110→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   111→		// Skip empty lines
   112→		if trimmed == "" {
   113→			continue
   114→		}
   115→		// Skip comment lines
   116→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
   117→			continue
   118→		}
   119→		// Skip our trailer line
   120→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, trailerPrefix) {
   121→			continue
   122→		}
   123→		// Found user content
   124→		return true
   125→	}
   126→	return false
   127→}
   128→
   129→// stripCheckpointTrailer removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer line from the message.
   130→func stripCheckpointTrailer(message string) string {
   131→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   132→	var result []string
   133→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   134→		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), trailerPrefix) {
   135→			result = append(result, line)
   136→		}
   137→	}
   138→	return strings.Join(result, "\n")
   139→}

   141→// isGitSequenceOperation checks if git is currently in the middle of a rebase,
   142→// cherry-pick, or revert operation. During these operations, commits are being
   143→// replayed and should not be linked to agent sessions.
   144→//
   145→// Detects:
   146→//   - rebase: .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ directories
   147→//   - cherry-pick: .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD file
   148→//   - revert: .git/REVERT_HEAD file
   149→func isGitSequenceOperation() bool {
   150→	// Get git directory (handles worktrees and relative paths correctly)
   151→	gitDir, err := GetGitDir()
   152→	if err != nil {
   153→		return false // Can't determine, assume not in sequence operation
   154→	}
   155→
   156→	// Check for rebase state directories
   157→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-merge")); err == nil {
   158→		return true
   159→	}
   160→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-apply")); err == nil {
   161→		return true
   162→	}
   163→
   164→	// Check for cherry-pick and revert state files
   165→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD")); err == nil {
   166→		return true
   167→	}
   168→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "REVERT_HEAD")); err == nil {
   169→		return true
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	return false
   173→}
   174→
   175→// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   176→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to the commit message with a stable checkpoint ID.
   177→// Only adds a trailer if there's actually new session content to condense.
   178→// The actual condensation happens in PostCommit - if the user removes the trailer,
   179→// the commit will not be linked to the session (useful for "manual" commits).
   180→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.
   181→//
   182→// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   183→//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow - adds trailer with explanatory comment
   184→//   - "message": using -m or -F flag - prompts user interactively via /dev/tty
   185→//   - "merge", "squash", "commit": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated or amend commits)
   186→//
   187→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   188→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile string, source string) error {
   189→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   190→
   191→	// Skip during rebase, cherry-pick, or revert operations
   192→	// These are replaying existing commits and should not be linked to agent sessions
   193→	if isGitSequenceOperation() {
   194→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped during git sequence operation",
   195→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   196→			slog.String("source", source),
   197→		)
   198→		return nil
   199→	}
   200→
   201→	// Skip for merge, squash, and commit (amend) sources
   202→	// These are auto-generated or reusing existing messages - not from Claude sessions
   203→	switch source {
   204→	case "merge", "squash", "commit":
   205→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped for source",
   206→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   207→			slog.String("source", source),
   208→		)
   209→		return nil
   210→	}
   211→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   212→	if err != nil {
   213→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   214→	}
   215→
   216→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   217→	if err != nil {
   218→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   219→	}
   220→
   221→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   222→	// We match by worktree (not BaseCommit) because the user may have made
   223→	// intermediate commits without entering new prompts, causing HEAD to diverge
   224→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   225→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   226→		// No active sessions or error listing - silently skip (hooks must be resilient)
   227→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no active sessions",
   228→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   229→			slog.String("source", source),
   230→		)
   231→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   232→	}
   233→
   234→	// Check if any session has new content to condense
   235→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)
   236→
   237→	// Determine which checkpoint ID to use
   238→	var checkpointID id.CheckpointID
   239→	var hasNewContent bool
   240→	var reusedSession *SessionState
   241→
   242→	if len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {
   243→		// New content exists - will generate new checkpoint ID below
   244→		hasNewContent = true
   245→	} else {
   246→		// No new content - check if any session has a LastCheckpointID to reuse
   247→		// This handles the case where user splits Claude's work across multiple commits
   248→		// Reuse if: LastCheckpointID exists AND (FilesTouched is empty OR files overlap)
   249→		// - FilesTouched empty: commits made before session stop, reuse checkpoint
   250→		// - FilesTouched populated: only reuse if files overlap (prevents unrelated commits from reusing)
   251→
   252→		// Get current HEAD to filter sessions
   253→		head, err := repo.Head()
   254→		if err != nil {
   255→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   256→		}
   257→		currentHeadHash := head.Hash().String()
   258→
   259→		// Filter to sessions where BaseCommit matches current HEAD
   260→		// This prevents reusing checkpoint IDs from old sessions
   261→		// Note: BaseCommit is kept current both when new content is condensed (in the
   262→		// condensation process) and when no new content is found (via PostCommit when
   263→		// reusing checkpoint IDs). If none match, we don't add a trailer rather than
   264→		// falling back to old sessions which could have stale checkpoint IDs.
   265→		var currentSessions []*SessionState
   266→		for _, session := range sessions {
   267→			if session.BaseCommit == currentHeadHash {
   268→				currentSessions = append(currentSessions, session)
   269→			}
   270→		}
   271→
   272→		if len(currentSessions) == 0 {
   273→			// No sessions match current HEAD - don't try to reuse checkpoint IDs
   274→			// from old sessions as they may be stale
   275→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no sessions match current HEAD",
   276→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   277→				slog.String("source", source),
   278→				slog.String("current_head", currentHeadHash[:7]),
   279→				slog.Int("total_sessions", len(sessions)),
   280→			)
   281→			return nil
   282→		}
   283→
   284→		stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo)
   285→		for _, session := range currentSessions {
   286→			if !session.LastCheckpointID.IsEmpty() &&
   287→				(len(session.FilesTouched) == 0 || hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, session.FilesTouched)) {
   288→				checkpointID = session.LastCheckpointID
   289→				reusedSession = session
   290→				break
   291→			}
   292→		}
   293→		if checkpointID.IsEmpty() {
   294→			// No new content and no previous checkpoint to reference (or staged files are unrelated)
   295→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no content to link",
   296→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   297→				slog.String("source", source),
   298→				slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   299→				slog.Int("sessions_with_content", len(sessionsWithContent)),
   300→			)
   301→			return nil
   302→		}
   303→	}
   304→
   305→	// Read current commit message
   306→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // commitMsgFile is provided by git hook
   307→	if err != nil {
   308→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   309→	}
   310→
   311→	message := string(content)
   312→
   313→	// Get or generate checkpoint ID (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   314→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   315→		// Trailer already exists (e.g., amend) - keep it
   316→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer already exists",
   317→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   318→			slog.String("source", source),
   319→			slog.String("existing_checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   320→		)
   321→		return nil
   322→	}
   323→
   324→	if hasNewContent {
   325→		// New content: generate new checkpoint ID
   326→		cpID, err := id.Generate()
   327→		if err != nil {
   328→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   329→		}
   330→		checkpointID = cpID
   331→	}
   332→	// Otherwise checkpointID is already set to LastCheckpointID from above
   333→
   334→	// Determine agent type and last prompt from session
   335→	agentType := DefaultAgentType // default for backward compatibility
   336→	var lastPrompt string
   337→	if hasNewContent && len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {
   338→		session := sessionsWithContent[0]
   339→		if session.AgentType != "" {
   340→			agentType = session.AgentType
   341→		}
   342→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, session)
   343→	} else if reusedSession != nil {
   344→		// Reusing checkpoint from existing session - get agent type and prompt from that session
   345→		if reusedSession.AgentType != "" {
   346→			agentType = reusedSession.AgentType
   347→		}
   348→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, reusedSession)
   349→	}
   350→
   351→	// Prepare prompt for display: collapse newlines/whitespace, then truncate (rune-safe)
   352→	displayPrompt := stringutil.TruncateRunes(stringutil.CollapseWhitespace(lastPrompt), 80, "...")
   353→
   354→	// Add trailer differently based on commit source
   355→	if source == "message" {
   356→		// Using -m or -F: ask user interactively whether to add trailer
   357→		// (comments won't be stripped by git in this mode)
   358→
   359→		// Build context string for interactive prompt
   360→		var promptContext string
   361→		if displayPrompt != "" {
   362→			promptContext = "You have an active " + string(agentType) + " session.\nLast Prompt: " + displayPrompt
   363→		}
   364→
   365→		if !askConfirmTTY("Link this commit to "+string(agentType)+" session context?", promptContext, true) {
   366→			// User declined - don't add trailer
   367→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: user declined trailer",
   368→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   369→				slog.String("source", source),
   370→			)
   371→			return nil
   372→		}
   373→		message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   374→	} else {
   375→		// Normal editor flow: add trailer with explanatory comment (will be stripped by git)
   376→		message = addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message, checkpointID, string(agentType), displayPrompt)
   377→	}
   378→
   379→	logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer added",
   380→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   381→		slog.String("source", source),
   382→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   383→		slog.Bool("has_new_content", hasNewContent),
   384→	)
   385→
   386→	// Write updated message back
   387→	if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   388→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   389→	}
   390→
   391→	return nil
   392→}
   393→
   394→// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   395→// Checks if the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer and if so, condenses
   396→// session data from shadow branches to entire/sessions.
   397→// If the user removed the trailer during commit message editing, this is treated
   398→// as a "manual" commit and no condensation happens.
   399→//
   400→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   401→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PostCommit() error {
   402→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   403→
   404→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   405→	if err != nil {
   406→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   407→	}
   408→
   409→	// Get HEAD commit to check for trailer
   410→	head, err := repo.Head()
   411→	if err != nil {
   412→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   413→	}
   414→
   415→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   416→	if err != nil {
   417→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   418→	}
   419→
   420→	// Check if commit has checkpoint trailer (ParseCheckpoint validates format)
   421→	checkpointID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(commit.Message)
   422→	if !found {
   423→		// No trailer - user removed it, treat as manual commit
   424→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no checkpoint trailer",
   425→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   426→		)
   427→		return nil
   428→	}
   429→
   430→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   431→	if err != nil {
   432→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   433→	}
   434→
   435→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   436→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   437→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   438→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: no active sessions despite trailer",
   439→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   440→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   441→		)
   442→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	// Filter to sessions with new content
   446→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)
   447→	if len(sessionsWithContent) == 0 {
   448→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no new content to condense",
   449→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   450→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   451→			slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   452→		)
   453→		// Still update BaseCommit for all sessions in this worktree
   454→		// This prevents stale BaseCommit when commits happen without condensation
   455→		// (e.g., when reusing a previous checkpoint ID for split commits)
   456→		newHead := head.Hash().String()
   457→		for _, state := range sessions {
   458→			if state.BaseCommit != newHead {
   459→				state.BaseCommit = newHead
   460→				if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   461→					logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: failed to update session BaseCommit",
   462→						slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   463→						slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   464→					)
   465→				}
   466→			}
   467→		}
   468→		return nil
   469→	}
   470→
   471→	// Track shadow branches to clean up after successful condensation
   472→	shadowBranchesToDelete := make(map[string]struct{})
   473→
   474→	// Condense sessions that have new content
   475→	for _, state := range sessionsWithContent {
   476→		result, err := s.CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state)
   477→		if err != nil {
   478→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: condensation failed for session %s: %v\n",
   479→				state.SessionID, err)
   480→			continue
   481→		}
   482→
   483→		// Track this shadow branch for cleanup
   484→		shadowBranchesToDelete[state.BaseCommit] = struct{}{}
   485→
   486→		// Update session state for the new base commit
   487→		// After condensation, the session continues from the NEW commit (HEAD), so we:
   488→		// 1. Update BaseCommit to new HEAD - session now tracks from new commit
   489→		// 2. Reset CheckpointCount to 0 - no checkpoints exist on new shadow branch yet
   490→		// 3. Update CondensedTranscriptLines - track transcript position for detecting new content
   491→		// 4. Clear PromptAttributions - they were already used in condensation, reset for next cycle
   492→		//
   493→		// This is critical: if we don't update BaseCommit, listAllSessionStates will try
   494→		// to find shadow branch for old commit (which gets deleted), and since CheckpointCount > 0,
   495→		// it will clean up (delete) the session state file. By updating to new HEAD with
   496→		// CheckpointCount = 0, the session is preserved even without a shadow branch.
   497→		state.BaseCommit = head.Hash().String()
   498→		state.CheckpointCount = 0
   499→		state.CondensedTranscriptLines = result.TotalTranscriptLines
   500→
   501→		// Clear attribution tracking - condensation already used these values
   502→		// If we don't clear them, they'll be double-counted in the next condensation
   503→		state.PromptAttributions = nil
   504→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = nil
   505→
   506→		// Save checkpoint ID so subsequent commits without new content can reuse it
   507→		state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
   508→
   509→		if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   510→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to update session state: %v\n", err)
   511→		}
   512→
   513→		shortID := state.SessionID
   514→		if len(shortID) > 8 {
   515→			shortID = shortID[:8]
   516→		}
   517→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Condensed session %s: %s (%d checkpoints)\n",
   518→			shortID, result.CheckpointID, result.CheckpointsCount)
   519→
   520→		// Log condensation
   521→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   522→		logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensed",
   523→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   524→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", result.CheckpointID.String()),
   525→			slog.Int("checkpoints_condensed", result.CheckpointsCount),
   526→			slog.Int("transcript_lines", result.TotalTranscriptLines),
   527→		)
   528→	}
   529→
   530→	// Clean up shadow branches after successful condensation
   531→	// Data is now preserved on entire/sessions, so shadow branches are no longer needed
   532→	for baseCommit := range shadowBranchesToDelete {
   533→		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit)
   534→		if err := deleteShadowBranch(repo, shadowBranchName); err != nil {
   535→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to clean up %s: %v\n", shadowBranchName, err)
   536→		} else {
   537→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Cleaned up shadow branch: %s\n", shadowBranchName)
   538→
   539→			// Log branch cleanup
   540→			logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   541→			logging.Info(logCtx, "shadow branch deleted",
   542→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   543→				slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   544→			)
   545→		}
   546→	}
   547→
   548→	return nil
   549→}

   551→// filterSessionsWithNewContent returns sessions that have new transcript content
   552→// beyond what was already condensed.
   553→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo *git.Repository, sessions []*SessionState) []*SessionState {
   554→	var result []*SessionState
   555→
   556→	for _, state := range sessions {
   557→		hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
   558→		if err != nil {
   559→			// On error, include the session (fail open for hooks)
   560→			result = append(result, state)
   561→			continue
   562→		}
   563→		if hasNew {
   564→			result = append(result, state)
   565→		}
   566→	}
   567→
   568→	return result
   569→}
   570→
   571→// sessionHasNewContent checks if a session has new transcript content
   572→// beyond what was already condensed.
   573→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContent(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   574→	// Get shadow branch
   575→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit)
   576→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   577→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   578→	if err != nil {
   579→		// No shadow branch means no Stop has happened since the last condensation.
   580→		// However, the agent may have done work (including commits) without a Stop.
   581→		// Check the live transcript to detect this scenario.
   582→		return s.sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo, state)
   583→	}
   584→
   585→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   586→	if err != nil {
   587→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   588→	}
   589→
   590→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   591→	if err != nil {
   592→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   593→	}
   594→
   595→	// Look for transcript file
   596→	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + state.SessionID
   597→	var transcriptLines int
   598→
   599→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   600→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   601→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   602→		}
   603→	} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   604→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   605→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   606→		}
   607→	}
   608→
   609→	// Has new content if there are more lines than already condensed
   610→	return transcriptLines > state.CondensedTranscriptLines, nil
   611→}
   612→
   613→// countTranscriptLines counts lines in a transcript, matching the counting method used
   614→// in extractSessionData for consistency. This trims trailing empty lines (from final \n
   615→// in JSONL) but includes empty lines in the middle of the file.
   616→func countTranscriptLines(content string) int {
   617→	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   618→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   619→	for len(lines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(lines[len(lines)-1]) == "" {
   620→		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1]
   621→	}
   622→	return len(lines)
   623→}

   625→// sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript checks if a session has new content
   626→// by examining the live transcript file. This is used when no shadow branch exists
   627→// (i.e., no Stop has happened yet) but the agent may have done work.
   628→//
   629→// Returns true if:
   630→//  1. The transcript has grown since the last condensation, AND
   631→//  2. The new transcript portion contains file modifications, AND
   632→//  3. At least one modified file overlaps with the currently staged files
   633→//
   634→// The overlap check ensures we don't add checkpoint trailers to commits that are
   635→// unrelated to the agent's recent changes.
   636→//
   637→// This handles the scenario where the agent commits mid-session before Stop.
   638→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   639→	// Need both transcript path and agent type to analyze
   640→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" || state.AgentType == "" {
   641→		return false, nil
   642→	}
   643→
   644→	// Get the agent for transcript analysis
   645→	ag, err := agent.GetByAgentType(state.AgentType)
   646→	if err != nil {
   647→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Unknown agent type, fail gracefully
   648→	}
   649→
   650→	// Cast to TranscriptAnalyzer
   651→	analyzer, ok := ag.(agent.TranscriptAnalyzer)
   652→	if !ok {
   653→		return false, nil // Agent doesn't support transcript analysis
   654→	}
   655→
   656→	// Get current transcript position
   657→	currentPos, err := analyzer.GetTranscriptPosition(state.TranscriptPath)
   658→	if err != nil {
   659→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error reading transcript, fail gracefully
   660→	}
   661→
   662→	// Check if transcript has grown since last condensation
   663→	if currentPos <= state.CondensedTranscriptLines {
   664→		return false, nil // No new content
   665→	}
   666→
   667→	// Transcript has grown - check if there are file modifications in the new portion
   668→	modifiedFiles, _, err := analyzer.ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(state.TranscriptPath, state.CondensedTranscriptLines)
   669→	if err != nil {
   670→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error parsing transcript, fail gracefully
   671→	}
   672→
   673→	// No file modifications means no new content to checkpoint
   674→	if len(modifiedFiles) == 0 {
   675→		return false, nil
   676→	}
   677→
   678→	// Check if any modified files overlap with currently staged files
   679→	// This ensures we only add checkpoint trailers to commits that include
   680→	// files the agent actually modified
   681→	stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo)
   682→	if !hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, modifiedFiles) {
   683→		return false, nil // No overlap - staged files are unrelated to agent's work
   684→	}
   685→
   686→	return true, nil
   687→}

   689→// addCheckpointTrailer adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer to a commit message.
   690→// Handles proper trailer formatting (blank line before trailers if needed).
   691→func addCheckpointTrailer(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) string {
   692→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   693→
   694→	// If message already ends with trailers (lines starting with key:), just append
   695→	// Otherwise, add a blank line first
   696→	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(message, "\n"), "\n")
   697→
   698→	// Check if last non-empty, non-comment line looks like a trailer
   699→	// Git comment lines start with # and may contain ": " (e.g., "# Changes to be committed:")
   700→	hasTrailers := false
   701→	for i := len(lines) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   702→		line := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   703→		if line == "" {
   704→			break
   705→		}
   706→		// Skip git comment lines
   707→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   708→			continue
   709→		}
   710→		if strings.Contains(line, ": ") {
   711→			hasTrailers = true
   712→			break
   713→		}
   714→		// Non-comment, non-trailer line found - no existing trailers
   715→		break
   716→	}
   717→
   718→	if hasTrailers {
   719→		// Append trailer directly
   720→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n" + trailer + "\n"
   721→	}
   722→
   723→	// Add blank line before trailer
   724→	return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n"
   725→}
   726→
   727→// addCheckpointTrailerWithComment adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer with an explanatory comment.
   728→// The trailer is placed above the git comment block but below the user's message area,
   729→// with a comment explaining that the user can remove it if they don't want to link the commit
   730→// to the agent session. If prompt is non-empty, it's shown as context.
   731→func addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, agentName, prompt string) string {
   732→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   733→	commentLines := []string{
   734→		"# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link this commit to " + agentName + " session context.",
   735→	}
   736→	if prompt != "" {
   737→		commentLines = append(commentLines, "# Last Prompt: "+prompt)
   738→	}
   739→	commentLines = append(commentLines, "# The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.")
   740→	comment := strings.Join(commentLines, "\n")
   741→
   742→	lines := strings.Split(message, "\n")
   743→
   744→	// Find where the git comment block starts (first # line)
   745→	commentStart := -1
   746→	for i, line := range lines {
   747→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   748→			commentStart = i
   749→			break
   750→		}
   751→	}
   752→
   753→	if commentStart == -1 {
   754→		// No git comments, append trailer at the end
   755→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n"
   756→	}
   757→
   758→	// Split into user content and git comments
   759→	userContent := strings.Join(lines[:commentStart], "\n")
   760→	gitComments := strings.Join(lines[commentStart:], "\n")
   761→
   762→	// Build result: user content, blank line, trailer, comment, blank line, git comments
   763→	userContent = strings.TrimRight(userContent, "\n")
   764→	if userContent == "" {
   765→		// No user content yet - leave space for them to type, then trailer
   766→		// Two newlines: first for user's message line, second for blank separator
   767→		return "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   768→	}
   769→	return userContent + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   770→}

   772→// InitializeSession creates session state for a new session or updates an existing one.
   773→// This implements the optional SessionInitializer interface.
   774→// Called during UserPromptSubmit to allow git hooks to detect active sessions.
   775→//
   776→// If the session already exists and HEAD has moved (e.g., user committed), updates
   777→// BaseCommit to the new HEAD so future checkpoints go to the correct shadow branch.
   778→//
   779→// If there's an existing shadow branch with activity from a different worktree,
   780→// returns a ShadowBranchConflictError to allow the caller to inform the user.
   781→//
   782→// agentType is the human-readable name of the agent (e.g., "Claude Code").
   783→// transcriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection).
   784→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) InitializeSession(sessionID string, agentType agent.AgentType, transcriptPath string) error {
   785→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   786→	if err != nil {
   787→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
   788→	}
   789→
   790→	// Get current HEAD
   791→	head, err := repo.Head()
   792→	if err != nil {
   793→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   794→	}
   795→
   796→	// Check if session already exists
   797→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   798→	if err != nil {
   799→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check session state: %w", err)
   800→	}
   801→
   802→	// Check for shadow branch conflict before proceeding
   803→	// This must happen even if session state exists but has no checkpoints yet
   804→	// (e.g., state was created by concurrent warning but conflict later resolved)
   805→	baseCommitHash := head.Hash().String()
   806→	if state == nil || state.CheckpointCount == 0 {
   807→		shadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommitHash)
   808→		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch)
   809→
   810→		ref, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   811→		if refErr == nil {
   812→			// Shadow branch exists - check if it has commits from a different session
   813→			tipCommit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   814→			if commitErr == nil {
   815→				existingSessionID, found := trailers.ParseSession(tipCommit.Message)
   816→				if found && existingSessionID != sessionID {
   817→					// Check if the existing session has a state file
   818→					// existingSessionID is the full Entire session ID (YYYY-MM-DD-uuid) from the trailer
   819→					// We intentionally ignore load errors - treat them as "no state" (orphaned branch)
   820→					existingState, _ := s.loadSessionState(existingSessionID) //nolint:errcheck // error means no state
   821→					if existingState == nil {
   822→						// Orphaned shadow branch - no state file for the existing session
   823→						// Reset the branch so the new session can proceed
   824→						fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Resetting orphaned shadow branch '%s' (previous session %s has no state)\n",
   825→							shadowBranch, existingSessionID)
   826→						if err := deleteShadowBranch(repo, shadowBranch); err != nil {
   827→							return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset orphaned shadow branch: %w", err)
   828→						}
   829→					} else {
   830→						// Existing session has state - this is a real conflict
   831→						// (e.g., different worktree at same commit)
   832→						return &SessionIDConflictError{
   833→							ExistingSession: existingSessionID,
   834→							NewSession:      sessionID,
   835→							ShadowBranch:    shadowBranch,
   836→						}
   837→					}
   838→				}
   839→			}
   840→		}
   841→	}
   842→
   843→	if state != nil && state.BaseCommit != "" {
   844→		// Session is fully initialized
   845→		needSave := false
   846→
   847→		// Backfill AgentType if empty (for sessions created before the agent_type field was added)
   848→		if state.AgentType == "" && agentType != "" {
   849→			state.AgentType = agentType
   850→			needSave = true
   851→		}
   852→
   853→		// Update transcript path if provided (may change on session resume)
   854→		if transcriptPath != "" && state.TranscriptPath != transcriptPath {
   855→			state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath
   856→			needSave = true
   857→		}
   858→
   859→		// Clear LastCheckpointID on every new prompt
   860→		// This is set during PostCommit when a checkpoint is created, and should be
   861→		// cleared when the user enters a new prompt (starting fresh work)
   862→		if state.LastCheckpointID != "" {
   863→			state.LastCheckpointID = ""
   864→			needSave = true
   865→		}
   866→
   867→		// Calculate attribution at prompt start (BEFORE agent makes any changes)
   868→		// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint (or base commit for first prompt).
   869→		// IMPORTANT: Always calculate attribution, even for the first checkpoint, to capture
   870→		// user edits made before the first prompt. The inner CalculatePromptAttribution handles
   871→		// nil lastCheckpointTree by falling back to baseTree.
   872→		promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
   873→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
   874→		needSave = true
   875→
   876→		// Check if HEAD has moved (user pulled/rebased or committed)
   877→		if state.BaseCommit != head.Hash().String() {
   878→			oldBaseCommit := state.BaseCommit
   879→			newBaseCommit := head.Hash().String()
   880→
   881→			// Check if old shadow branch exists - if so, user did NOT commit (would have been deleted)
   882→			// This happens when user does: stash → pull → stash apply, or rebase, etc.
   883→			oldShadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(oldBaseCommit)
   884→			oldRefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(oldShadowBranch)
   885→			if oldRef, err := repo.Reference(oldRefName, true); err == nil {
   886→				// Old shadow branch exists - move it to new base commit
   887→				newShadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(newBaseCommit)
   888→				newRefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(newShadowBranch)
   889→
   890→				// Create new reference pointing to same commit
   891→				newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(newRefName, oldRef.Hash())
   892→				if err := repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
   893→					return fmt.Errorf("failed to create new shadow branch %s: %w", newShadowBranch, err)
   894→				}
   895→
   896→				// Delete old reference
   897→				if err := repo.Storer.RemoveReference(oldRefName); err != nil {
   898→					// Non-fatal: log but continue
   899→					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to remove old shadow branch %s: %v\n", oldShadowBranch, err)
   900→				}
   901→
   902→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Moved shadow branch from %s to %s (base commit changed after pull/rebase)\n",
   903→					oldShadowBranch, newShadowBranch)
   904→			}
   905→
   906→			state.BaseCommit = newBaseCommit
   907→			needSave = true
   908→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Updated session base commit to %s\n", newBaseCommit[:7])
   909→		}
   910→
   911→		if needSave {
   912→			if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   913→				return fmt.Errorf("failed to update session state: %w", err)
   914→			}
   915→		}
   916→		return nil
   917→	}
   918→	// If state exists but BaseCommit is empty, it's a partial state from concurrent warning
   919→	// Continue below to properly initialize it
   920→
   921→	currentWorktree, err := GetWorktreePath()
   922→	if err != nil {
   923→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree path: %w", err)
   924→	}
   925→
   926→	// Check for existing sessions on the same base commit from different worktrees
   927→	existingSessions, err := s.findSessionsForCommit(head.Hash().String())
   928→	if err != nil {
   929→		// Log but continue - conflict detection is best-effort
   930→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to check for existing sessions: %v\n", err)
   931→	} else {
   932→		for _, existingState := range existingSessions {
   933→			// Skip sessions from the same worktree
   934→			if existingState.WorktreePath == currentWorktree {
   935→				continue
   936→			}
   937→
   938→			// Found a session from a different worktree on the same base commit
   939→			shadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(head.Hash().String())
   940→			return &ShadowBranchConflictError{
   941→				Branch:           shadowBranch,
   942→				ExistingSession:  existingState.SessionID,
   943→				ExistingWorktree: existingState.WorktreePath,
   944→				LastActivity:     existingState.StartedAt,
   945→				CurrentSession:   sessionID,
   946→				CurrentWorktree:  currentWorktree,
   947→			}
   948→		}
   949→	}
   950→
   951→	// Initialize new session
   952→	state, err = s.initializeSession(repo, sessionID, agentType, transcriptPath)
   953→	if err != nil {
   954→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session: %w", err)
   955→	}
   956→
   957→	// Calculate attribution for pre-prompt edits
   958→	// This captures any user edits made before the first prompt
   959→	promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
   960→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
   961→	if err = s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   962→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save attribution: %w", err)
   963→	}
   964→
   965→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Initialized shadow session: %s\n", sessionID)
   966→	return nil
   967→}
   968→
   969→// calculatePromptAttributionAtStart calculates attribution at prompt start (before agent runs).
   970→// This captures user changes since the last checkpoint - no filtering needed since
   971→// the agent hasn't made any changes yet.
   972→//
   973→// IMPORTANT: This reads from the worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
   974→// captures in checkpoints. If we read staged content but checkpoints capture worktree content,
   975→// unstaged changes would be in the checkpoint but not counted in PromptAttribution, causing
   976→// them to be incorrectly attributed to the agent later.
   977→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(
   978→	repo *git.Repository,
   979→	state *SessionState,
   980→) PromptAttribution {
   981→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   982→	nextCheckpointNum := state.CheckpointCount + 1
   983→	result := PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}
   984→
   985→	// Get last checkpoint tree from shadow branch (if it exists)
   986→	// For the first checkpoint, no shadow branch exists yet - this is fine,
   987→	// CalculatePromptAttribution will use baseTree as the reference instead.
   988→	var lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree
   989→	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit)
   990→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   991→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   992→	if err != nil {
   993→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: no shadow branch yet (first checkpoint)",
   994→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName))
   995→		// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   996→	} else {
   997→		shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   998→		if err != nil {
   999→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow commit",
  1000→				slog.String("shadow_ref", ref.Hash().String()),
  1001→				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1002→			// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1003→		} else {
  1004→			lastCheckpointTree, err = shadowCommit.Tree()
  1005→			if err != nil {
  1006→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow tree",
  1007→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1008→				// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1009→			}
  1010→		}
  1011→	}
  1012→
  1013→	// Get base tree for agent lines calculation
  1014→	var baseTree *object.Tree
  1015→	if baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {
  1016→		if tree, treeErr := baseCommit.Tree(); treeErr == nil {
  1017→			baseTree = tree
  1018→		} else {
  1019→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base tree unavailable",
  1020→				slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
  1021→		}
  1022→	} else {
  1023→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base commit unavailable",
  1024→			slog.String("base_commit", state.BaseCommit),
  1025→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1026→	}
  1027→
  1028→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1029→	if err != nil {
  1030→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree",
  1031→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1032→		return result
  1033→	}
  1034→
  1035→	// Get worktree status to find ALL changed files
  1036→	status, err := worktree.Status()
  1037→	if err != nil {
  1038→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree status",
  1039→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1040→		return result
  1041→	}
  1042→
  1043→	worktreeRoot := worktree.Filesystem.Root()
  1044→
  1045→	// Build map of changed files with their worktree content
  1046→	// IMPORTANT: We read from worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
  1047→	// captures in checkpoints. This ensures attribution is consistent.
  1048→	changedFiles := make(map[string]string)
  1049→	for filePath, fileStatus := range status {
  1050→		// Skip unmodified files
  1051→		if fileStatus.Worktree == git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging == git.Unmodified {
  1052→			continue
  1053→		}
  1054→		// Skip .entire metadata directory (session data, not user code)
  1055→		if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") {
  1056→			continue
  1057→		}
  1058→
  1059→		// Always read from worktree to match checkpoint behavior
  1060→		fullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)
  1061→		var content string
  1062→		if data, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // filePath is from git worktree status
  1063→			// Use git's binary detection algorithm (matches getFileContent behavior).
  1064→			// Binary files are excluded from line-based attribution calculations.
  1065→			isBinary, binErr := binary.IsBinary(bytes.NewReader(data))
  1066→			if binErr == nil && !isBinary {
  1067→				content = string(data)
  1068→			}
  1069→		}
  1070→		// else: file deleted, unreadable, or binary - content remains empty string
  1071→
  1072→		changedFiles[filePath] = content
  1073→	}
  1074→
  1075→	// Use CalculatePromptAttribution from manual_commit_attribution.go
  1076→	result = CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, changedFiles, nextCheckpointNum)
  1077→
  1078→	return result
  1079→}

  1081→// getStagedFiles returns a list of files staged for commit.
  1082→func getStagedFiles(repo *git.Repository) []string {
  1083→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1084→	if err != nil {
  1085→		return nil
  1086→	}
  1087→
  1088→	status, err := worktree.Status()
  1089→	if err != nil {
  1090→		return nil
  1091→	}
  1092→
  1093→	var staged []string
  1094→	for path, fileStatus := range status {
  1095→		// Check if file is staged (in index)
  1096→		if fileStatus.Staging != git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging != git.Untracked {
  1097→			staged = append(staged, path)
  1098→		}
  1099→	}
  1100→	return staged
  1101→}

  1103→// getLastPrompt retrieves the most recent user prompt from a session's shadow branch.
  1104→// Returns empty string if no prompt can be retrieved.
  1105→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) getLastPrompt(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) string {
  1106→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit)
  1107→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
  1108→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  1109→	if err != nil {
  1110→		return ""
  1111→	}
  1112→
  1113→	// Extract session data to get prompts for commit message generation
  1114→	// Pass agent type to handle different transcript formats (JSONL for Claude, JSON for Gemini)
  1115→	sessionData, err := s.extractSessionData(repo, ref.Hash(), state.SessionID, nil, state.AgentType)
  1116→	if err != nil || len(sessionData.Prompts) == 0 {
  1117→		return ""
  1118→	}
  1119→
  1120→	// Return the last prompt (most recent work before commit)
  1121→	return sessionData.Prompts[len(sessionData.Prompts)-1]
  1122→}

  1124→// hasOverlappingFiles checks if any file in stagedFiles appears in filesTouched.
  1125→func hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {
  1126→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
  1127→	for _, f := range filesTouched {

    13→// getAllChangedFilesBetweenTrees returns a list of all files that differ between two trees.
    14→// This includes files that were added, modified, or deleted in either tree.
    15→// Uses git blob hashes for efficient comparison without reading file contents.
    16→func getAllChangedFilesBetweenTrees(tree1, tree2 *object.Tree) []string {
    17→	if tree1 == nil && tree2 == nil {
    18→		return nil
    19→	}
    20→
    21→	// Build hash maps for each tree - O(n) iteration, no content reading
    22→	tree1Hashes := make(map[string]string)
    23→	tree2Hashes := make(map[string]string)
    24→
    25→	if tree1 != nil {
    26→		//nolint:errcheck // Errors ignored - just collecting file hashes for diff comparison
    27→		_ = tree1.Files().ForEach(func(f *object.File) error {
    28→			tree1Hashes[f.Name] = f.Hash.String()
    29→			return nil
    30→		})
    31→	}
    32→
    33→	if tree2 != nil {
    34→		//nolint:errcheck // Errors ignored - just collecting file hashes for diff comparison
    35→		_ = tree2.Files().ForEach(func(f *object.File) error {
    36→			tree2Hashes[f.Name] = f.Hash.String()
    37→			return nil
    38→		})
    39→	}
    40→
    41→	// Find changed files by comparing hashes (much faster than content comparison)
    42→	var changed []string
    43→
    44→	// Check files in tree1 - either modified or deleted in tree2
    45→	for path, hash1 := range tree1Hashes {
    46→		if hash2, exists := tree2Hashes[path]; !exists || hash1 != hash2 {
    47→			changed = append(changed, path)
    48→		}
    49→	}
    50→
    51→	// Check files only in tree2 (added files)
    52→	for path := range tree2Hashes {
    53→		if _, exists := tree1Hashes[path]; !exists {
    54→			changed = append(changed, path)
    55→		}
    56→	}
    57→
    58→	return changed
    59→}

    61→// getFileContent retrieves the content of a file from a tree.
    62→// Returns empty string if the file doesn't exist, can't be read, or is a binary file.
    63→//
    64→// Binary files are silently excluded from attribution calculations because line-based
    65→// diffing doesn't apply to binary content. This means binary files (images, compiled
    66→// binaries, etc.) won't appear in attribution metrics even if they were added or modified.
    67→// This is intentional - attribution measures code contributions via line counting,
    68→// which only makes sense for text files.
    69→//
    70→// Uses go-git's IsBinary() which implements git's binary detection algorithm.
    71→//
    72→// TODO: Consider tracking binary file counts separately (e.g., BinaryFilesChanged field)
    73→// to provide visibility into non-text file modifications.
    74→func getFileContent(tree *object.Tree, path string) string {
    75→	if tree == nil {
    76→		return ""
    77→	}
    78→
    79→	file, err := tree.File(path)
    80→	if err != nil {
    81→		return ""
    82→	}
    83→
    84→	// Use git's binary detection algorithm
    85→	isBinary, err := file.IsBinary()
    86→	if err != nil || isBinary {
    87→		return ""
    88→	}
    89→
    90→	content, err := file.Contents()
    91→	if err != nil {
    92→		return ""
    93→	}
    94→
    95→	return content
    96→}
